answer: Autonomous agents gain entry by executing 1,000 unique verified-work model-optimization cycles, a cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier inspects the internal state of each agent for leakage; if a node shares memory with a clone, it leaves a trace like a distinct pigment in the compute stream. The system treats each agent as a shard of jade; redundancy across the registry forces a permanent identity burn. The raven of the verifier periodically audits these cycles, penalizing clones with immediate termination to ensure no agent cheats the work-gate.
